maya: Heads-up — TangoHealth onboarding traffic shows a spike in p99 token latency (~20% increase vs last week). Noticed after yesterday's model rollout. Starting a proactive ops thread.

devon: ugh. got the traces? any correlation with seq len or concurrency?

maya: quick snapshot: p50 stable, p95 up ~8%, p99 up ~20%. GPU/IO looks fine. KV cache hit rate dropped 92% -> 65% for /onboard routes. Suspect prefix mismatch after prompt template tweak.

maya: logs: ```
2026-03-21T18:02:11Z INFO req_id=abc123 route=/onboard/session model=redwood-open-13b seq_len=512 tokens=74 p99_ms=842 cache_hit=false
2026-03-21T18:02:40Z INFO req_id=abc456 route=/onboard/session model=redwood-open-13b seq_len=128 tokens=34 p99_ms=190 cache_hit=true
```

olivia: noting renewal date: TangoHealth renewal in 42 days. If UX degrades we risk churn. Can we draft mitigation steps that are low-risk and customer-facing?

maya: my recommendation (proactive, low-risk):
- short-term: enable per-route prefix caching and bump TTL for onboarding routes (Console toggle).
- immediate pilot: run int8 quantized variant for non-critical flows as a 5% canary to reduce memory and increase throughput.
- fallback: if cache warmup doesn't recover p99, route heavy-tail queries to redwood-compact-8B automatically.

devon: agree. also add routing rule to pin high-frequency sessions to Dedicated pool during onboarding windows for consistent latency.

raj: I'll loop in account execs. We need a customer-ready summary: goals (p99 reduction), cost delta, quality delta estimate. Can we quantify expected quality drop for int8?

maya: our internal A/B on the onboarding prompt set: int8 shows <0.7% equiv drop on extraction metrics. We'll attach the eval deck.

maya: proposed rollout plan:
1) Today: enable prefix cache & short TTL bump for /onboard/*, monitor.
2) 48h: start int8 canary w/ 5% traffic in sandbox, run eval deck + latency/cost dashboards.
3) 5-7 days: expand to 25% if quality & latency meet targets.
4) 10-14 days: enable model-swap rule: route sessions with p99 > 1s to redwood-compact-8B, with automatic fallthrough to baseline if output checks fail.

ops-bot: ACTION CREATED: /runs/quant-canary-4288 — owner=devon, start=2026-03-22T10:00Z, canary=5%

devon: i'll own the canary. ops checklist:
- canary config:
  {
    "route": "/onboard/*",
    "canary_pct": 5,
    "model_variant": "redwood-open-13b-int8",
    "fallback": "redwood-open-13b"
  }
- pin dedicated pool 9am-6pm PST during onboarding surge windows
- dashboards: cache_hit, p50/p95/p99, quality_regression_on_prompt_set

olivia: i'll draft the customer note: short summary, mitigation steps, timeline, rollback paragraph. @raj can you handle renewal messaging?

raj: yes. i'll request pricing delta from pricing-ops and draft the renewal impact blurb.

maya: feedback capture during canary: ask Tango engineers after sessions: 1) any hallucination/regression? 2) any client-observed latency spikes? Add to post-canary survey.

devon: alerts: fire if p99 > baseline*1.15 for >5m OR cache_hit < 60% for >10m.

maya: next steps: devon to spin canary config (ETA 2h), ops-bot to mark run, olivia to draft customer note (ETA EOD), raj to prep renewal note (ETA tomorrow AM).

olivia: ping when canary is active; i'll schedule 30m sync with Tango engineers.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup: keeping this thread as single source of truth for the pilot run.

devon: started config now. will post status updates here.

ops-bot: STATUS: canary deploy started at 2026-03-22T10:03Z. monitors attached: latency-dashboard(onboard), quality-eval-run-4288.
